questions.question: Your build outputs app.3f9a1c.js (hashed) and index.html. What caching strategy is correct?
options: Long, immutable cache for the hashed JS; no cache for index.html
Cache index.html for one year and the JS for zero seconds
questions.explanation: A new build changes the hash in the file name, so hashed assets can be cached forever. index.html must stay fresh so browsers learn the new asset names.

questions.question: In EJS, what is the difference between <%= value %> and <%- value %>?
options: <%= %> HTML-escapes the output; <%- %> outputs raw, unescaped HTML
<%= %> runs JavaScript without output; <%- %> prints it
<%- %> escapes the output; <%= %> prints raw HTML
questions.explanation: Use <%= %> for anything user-supplied. <%- %> is only for trusted markup such as partials; using it on user input creates an XSS vulnerability.

questions.question: In Express 5, which route path serves index.html for every client-side route including the root "/"?
questions.explanation: Express 5 requires named wildcards. "/*splat" needs at least one segment, so it misses "/"; wrapping it in braces makes it optional and matches the root too.

questions.question: Why should you pass an absolute path, e.g. built from import.meta.dirname, to express.static?
options: A relative path resolves against the process's working directory, which breaks when the app is started from another folder
questions.explanation: Relative paths depend on where node was launched, not where the file lives. An absolute path built from the module's directory is stable.
